analysis.title: The CEO Macro Briefing Book 4Q26 summary: After the hike, ahead of the vote
key_insights: Economic activity and the outlook remain robust despite higher oil prices and higher interest rates, amid an AI-led economic boom.
Spending is driven by strong balance sheets rather than income growth. Wage growth is sluggish, while strong demand and higher prices have pushed nominal spending higher.
After the midterm election, the legislative bar to meaningfully slow AI investment is very high in either a 'Split Congress' or 'Blue Wave' case.
Growth tracking implies an acceleration for 3Q, while inflation stayed stubbornly above the 2% target.
The Fed is expected to hike at least two more times before a dovish pivot in 2027.
Consumer spending is stable in aggregate, with growing evidence that higher-income households dominate it.
The labor market shows resilience with low unemployment. Financing conditions are tightening with higher rates.
Large-cap equities held up well in 3Q, while interest-rate-sensitive smaller caps lagged. Dealmaking is headed for a strong year despite softness in 3Q.
UBS CIO forecasts for June 2027: S&P 500 at 5,200, Fed funds rate 4.5%, 10Y Treasury yield 4.8%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: UBS CIO forecast for June 2027. The report expects at least two more Fed hikes before a dovish pivot in 2027.
UBS CIO forecast for June 2027, consistent with tightening financing conditions.
Inflation stayed stubbornly above target, supporting further Fed hikes.
Growth tracking implies a quarterly acceleration for 3Q.

risk_factors: Higher oil prices and higher interest rates.
Tightening financing conditions, which weigh on interest-rate-sensitive smaller caps.
Consumer spending increasingly concentrated in higher-income households, with sluggish wage growth.
Inflation stubbornly above target, with at least two more Fed hikes expected.
Midterm election outcome (Split Congress or Blue Wave), though the legislative bar to slow AI investment is high.
geopolitical: Higher oil prices are cited as a headwind that the economy has absorbed. The report gives no further detail on the cause.
